exposure: Retrospective subjective appraisal of birth pain
Medically documented measures of pain during labor
Quality of provider communication during labor
outcome: Postpartum-onset PTSD (probable PTSD at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum)
cohort: A sample of 112 women who screened positive for psychopathology within a year postpartum.
finding: Positive perception of birth pain was associated with reduced risk of probable PTSD at 6 weeks postpartum, and positive provider communication was associated with reduced risk of probable PTSD at 6 months and 12 months postpartum, while objective pain scores recorded during labor were not significantly associated with PTSD.
cross-section timing: Interviews were conducted within a year postpartum, assessing subjective labor experiences and associations with PTSD at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum.
